question: A and B can do a piece of work in 28 days; B and C can do the same work in 18 days and A, B and C together can do it in 16 days. The time required (in days) to finish the work by A and C is:
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = LCM(28, 18, 16) = 1008 units

Efficiency of (A + B + C) = 1008 ÷ 16 = 63 units/day

Efficiency of A = 63 − (1008 ÷ 18) = 63 − 56 = 7 units/day

Efficiency of C = 63 − (1008 ÷ 28) = 63 − 36 = 27 units/day

Time taken by (A + C) = 1008 ÷ (7 + 27) = 1008 ÷ 34 = 504 ÷ 17 = 29¹¹/₁₇ days

**∴ The correct answer is 29¹¹/₁₇ days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A and B = 28 days

Time taken by B and C = 18 days

Time taken by A, B and C together = 16 days

⇒ Efficiency of A = Efficiency of (A + B + C) − Efficiency of (B + C)

⇒ Efficiency of A = 63 − 56 = 7 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of C = Efficiency of (A + B + C) − Efficiency of (A + B)

⇒ Efficiency of C = 63 − 36 = 27 units/day

⇒ Combined efficiency of A and C = 7 + 27 = 34 units/day

⇒ Time required by A and C = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency

⇒ Time required = 1008 ÷ 34 = 504 ÷ 17 days

⇒ Time required = 29¹¹/₁₇ days

**∴ The correct answer is 29¹¹/₁₇ days.**

**__Additional Information__**

Total Work Concept

Total work is considered as the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the given individual times taken by each person or group.

Efficiency Formula

Efficiency is defined as the total work done per unit time. Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time taken.

Combined Work

When multiple people work together, their combined total efficiency is always the sum of their individual efficiencies.
